correctness.rationale: Halmos principal-angle reduction gives each generic 2x2 block eigenvalues 1+/-t of P+Q, t^2 of PQP, and squared commutator 2t^2(1-t^2). For 3<=p<4 the normalized f_p(x) has strictly positive second derivative because binomial coefficients binom(p,2k) for k>=2 are nonnegative and -(2^p-2)x^((p-2)/2) is strictly convex; for 4<p<=5 all nonlinear binomial terms are nonpositive and the negative power is strictly concave. The anchored secant quotient is monotone with sign reversal. Its limits are p(p-1)/2 and p(2^(p-1)-2)/4, giving both sharp constants; two-dimensional principal-angle witnesses attain both limits. Integer endpoints and p=4 exact identity checked. 20300 finite diagnostic tests additionally passed, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The previously known nonnegative complementary trace deficit does not measure the size of noncommutativity. The complete best two-sided dimension-free comparison with squared commutator energy supplies a quantitative stability law over an interval of noninteger exponents, with a genuine change in which limiting geometry controls the sharp estimate at fourth power. It is motivated by the exact complementary trace inequality and has a natural optimal invariant rather than arbitrary parameter slicing. The quartic specialization is known, credited, and not the novel contribution.
